API errors and rate limits

Source: vignettes/articles/troubleshooting.Rmd
troubleshooting.Rmd

The BFS API is not available

Sometimes an API does not answer. For example, you sent too many requests (HTTP 429), the API is too slow (timeout), or the server has a problem. Then the functions give an error that starts with “The BFS API is not available.”:

Error:
! The BFS API is not available.
ℹ HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
Caused by error in `httr2::req_perform()`:
! HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.

If you have no internet connection, the functions give the message “No internet connection” and return NULL.

Too many requests

The PXWeb API accepts only a limited number of requests from each IP address in a given time (see its configuration). bfs_get_data() sends two requests: one for the variables of the dataset, and one for the data. If you use it in a loop:

  • Wait between the calls, for example with delay = 10 (seconds) or Sys.sleep().
  • Save the results. Don’t download the same data again.

If you still get the error, the dataset may be too big for the API. Then download only a part of it with query (see Data catalog and PXWeb datasets), or the whole PX file with bfs_download_asset() (see Tables and files).

Handle the errors in your code

These errors have the class bfs_http_error. So you can handle them in your code, for example to try again later or to skip a dataset:

data <- tryCatch(
  bfs_get_data(number_bfs = "px-x-1502040100_131", language = "en"),
  bfs_http_error = function(e) {
    message("Skipped: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)

The error also keeps its original classes and fields. For example, you can use httr2_http_429 with the response in e$resp, or http_429 for the errors of the pxweb package:

tryCatch(
  bfs_sse_dimensions("DF_LWZ_1"),
  httr2_http_429 = function(e) httr2::resp_retry_after(e$resp)
)

You also find the original error in e$parent.

Caches

The package keeps some data, so it does not download it again (a cache):

  • The base maps of bfs_get_base_maps() are saved on your disk.
  • The list of the Swiss Stats Explorer datasets of bfs_get_sse_data() and bfs_get_sse_metadata() is kept during your R session. bfs_sse_datasets(), bfs_sse_dimensions() and bfs_sse_data() keep nothing: they always get the latest data.

If a base map or a new dataset is missing, clear the cache with bfs_clear_cache().
